channel.title: The Darker Reel: Dark History, Propaganda and Prejudice from Government Films
channel.description: The darker side of the twentieth century as the government's own films told it: prejudice and persecution, propaganda, fear, crime and the machinery of control. Each episode narrates a public-domain U.S. government film against its own words, with quoted lines read in a second voice, and keeps the film's framing: who is speaking, who the film is about, and when. Episodes come from Cinema of the Underground. The narration voice is synthetic; the archival film is unaltered. Keywords: world war 2 history, propaganda, psychological warfare, prejudice, history of war, war history, government films, archival film.
channel.itunes:author: Cinema of the Underground

item.title: Don't Be a Sucker (1947): how prejudice divided Germany
item.description: Don't Be a Sucker is a 1947 U.S. War Department film. It opens on an American street, where a speaker selling a pamphlet turns a crowd against its neighbours, then follows an older man's account of Berlin in 1932: how the Nazis used prejudice as a weapon to divide Germany, what they promised five young men in one crowd, and what those promises came to. Everything said here comes from the film's own narration and dialogue; lines quoted from the film are read in a second voice. The narration voice is synthetic; the archival film is unaltered. Source: U.S. War Department, Educational Film E.F. 6, public domain.
